group: The Supernatural: The Devil, Demons & Angels
belief: I should pray to angels for help.
meta: A Christian look at the false belief that you should pray to angels for help, with Scripture, questions, and homework for replacing it with the truth.
origins: Popular books, gift items, and media that encourage “calling on your angels.” Feeling that God is too big or distant to bother, while angels seem closer and more approachable. New Age spirituality mixed with Christian language. A sincere desire for protection and comfort. Not knowing what the Bible teaches about angels.
teaches: Angels are real, and God sends them to serve and guard His people. But Scripture never directs us to pray to them. When John fell down before an angel, the angel stopped him: “Worship God!” Paul warned against the worship of angels. Jesus taught us to pray to “our Father in heaven.” You can bring every need directly to God, and He is able to command His angels as He sees fit.
self_statements: My angels will protect me if I ask them.
God is too busy, so I’ll ask an angel.
Angels are easier to talk to than God.
I need to call on the right angel for this problem.
Praying to angels is just extra help.
God won’t mind if I go to them instead.
errors: Adopting popular beliefs about angels without testing them by Scripture.
Picturing God as too distant or busy to hear you directly.
Deciding a practice is right because it feels comforting.
Blending true facts about angels with practices Scripture warns against.
questions: What did the angel say when John fell down before him?
Who did Jesus teach us to pray to?
Where in the Bible does anyone pray to an angel?
Why would I go to a servant when I can go to the King, who is my Father?
Is God really too busy for my prayers?
Where did I learn to pray to angels: Scripture or popular culture?
truth: I do not need to pray to angels. I can pray directly to my Father in heaven, who hears me and cares for me. Angels are real, and God sends them to serve His people, but they point me to worship God, not themselves. I can thank God for His angels and bring every request to Him.
hw_questions: What did the angel tell John to do?
Who did Jesus teach me to pray to?
Does anyone in the Bible pray to angels?
Why go to a servant when I can go to my Father?
Did I learn this from Scripture or from culture?
hw_truths: I can pray directly to my Father in heaven.
God hears me and is never too busy for me.
Angels serve God and point me to worship Him.
God commands His angels to guard me as He wills.
I bring every request to God with thanksgiving.
log: Each day, write one request I brought directly to God and anything I noticed afterward.
name_example: For He will command His angels concerning Sarah to guard her in all her ways.
actions: Each time you are tempted to call on an angel,
pray instead, “Father, You know what I need,” and name it.
Remove one item, book, or app
that encourages praying to angels, and replace it with a Scripture card.
Read every passage about angels in Hebrews 1
and write down what angels are for.
Pray the Lord’s Prayer slowly each morning this week,
noticing who it is addressed to.
tracker: One request I brought to God
prayer: Our Father in heaven, thank You that I can come to You directly. Help me reject the idea that I should pray to angels. Thank You for the angels You send to serve Your people, and help me give all my worship and trust to You alone. You hear me, and You care for me. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
